plan.title: Reasoning effort, end to end: one resolver, set on every launch surface, persisted, visible, changeable live, and per-tier
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-5-5

metadata.sizeJustification: 25 files, at the 25-file cap. Only three code subsystems are touched (packages/contracts, src/lib, src/cli). The other six 'subsystems' the first-two-segment counter reports are single top-level files: package.json, docs.json, scripts/lint-effort.sh, configuration/effort.mdx, docs/CONFIGURATION.md and docs/MODEL-CONTEXT-AUDIT.md. The full effort program was already decomposed into eight sibling issues (#4253-#4260); this plan is only the foundation slice.

narratives.Problem: Reasoning effort is resolved ad hoc in about 13 places, each with its own `?? 'high'` fallback, and the level enum is copied at least 10 times. roles.<role>.effort is validated for every role but read only by `pan start` for work; sub-roles, tiers and projects carry no effort; config validation is duplicated between config-yaml/roles.ts and settings-api.ts; and an explicit unsupported level hard-fails instead of clamping. Every other effort gap (relaunch, conversations, live change, role surfaces, tier slots, planning, visibility, harness mapping) needs one resolver and one enum first.
narratives.Proposal: Ship the foundation of the effort program here and the surfaces in eight sibling issues (#4253-#4260). Add one EffortLevel/EFFORT_LEVELS in packages/contracts/src/effort.ts plus per-harness effortLevels on HarnessBehavior; add resolveEffort() in src/lib/agents/resolve-effort.ts with the precedence explicit > item > plan > tier > sub-role > role > project > default 'high' and model∩harness clamping; add effort to sub-roles, tiers and projects with one shared validator; wire `pan start` and the three runtime-command.ts fallbacks (definition-less role runs, codex and omp launcher fields) through the resolver; add a lint:effort ratchet; and document it all in configuration/effort.mdx.
narratives.NonGoals:
- No changes under src/dashboard/ (frontend or server); those belong to siblings #4254, #4255, #4256, #4257, #4258, #4259
- No new per-issue record, database column or issue-record field for effort; the per-issue override lives in the xBRIEF (plan.metadata.effort, item metadata.effort)
- No persistence of effort on AgentState, conversations, the cost ledger or sessions.json (siblings #4253, #4254, #4259)
- No change to how swarm/foreman/tier slots or escalation pick effort; tier effort is validated and resolvable only (sibling #4257)
- No change to the planning-effort path at start.ts:904 or to pan plan (sibling #4258)
- No removal of harness-adapter fallbacks outside runtime-command.ts (sibling #4260)
- No change to sync-sources/rules/effort-high-default.md or to roles/*.md frontmatter
- No xhigh or max default anywhere

autoDecisions.summary: Decompose into a foundation slice (this issue) plus eight sibling issues #4253-#4260, filed during planning and each blocked by #4249.
autoDecisions.rationale: The full program touches about 70 files across six code areas, and the plan-finalize surface lint caps one plan at 25 files. The audit already groups the work by launch surface, so each surface is an independently shippable vertical slice.

autoDecisions.summary: The per-issue effort override lives in the xBRIEF as plan.metadata.effort, with per-item metadata.effort above it, not on an issue record.
autoDecisions.rationale: PAN-3917 removed per-issue records by design (resolveIssueWorkModel now always returns undefined). The xBRIEF is committed in git and derivable, and it is already the home of plan.metadata.tiered_execution and the per-bead metadata.model override.

autoDecisions.summary: resolveEffort takes an already-resolved tierName instead of a difficulty.
autoDecisions.rationale: resolveTier already maps difficulty to a tier, so re-resolving it inside the effort resolver would duplicate tier logic and could disagree with staffing.

autoDecisions.summary: The resolver clamps canonical to canonical against model levels ∩ HarnessBehavior.effortLevels. Harness-native translation (Kimi, opencode) stays in adapters.
autoDecisions.rationale: Clamping is policy that every launch shares. Translation is a per-harness wire detail. Keeping them apart keeps the resolver's output a canonical EffortLevel.

autoDecisions.summary: Config values the configured model cannot run are still rejected at load. Explicit runtime values (pan start --effort) are clamped with a stderr warning. Non-canonical explicit values still exit 1.
autoDecisions.rationale: This keeps the existing config-yaml-roles and settings-api tests valid while meeting the issue's clamp-with-warning goal for runtime input.

autoDecisions.summary: Per-harness supported levels live on HarnessBehavior.effortLevels in packages/contracts. Only ohmypi and muse are restricted (no max).
autoDecisions.rationale: harness-behavior.ts is the existing per-harness capability table. The audit shows omp --thinking and muse --reasoning-effort both stop at xhigh.

autoDecisions.summary: The lint:effort ratchet fails only when a file's count rises above its baseline. A lower count prints a note instead of failing.
autoDecisions.rationale: Eight siblings will lower counts in parallel, and a strict-equality ratchet would make each of them conflict on baseline lines.

autoDecisions.summary: The effort-high-default rule wording and roles/*.md frontmatter stay unchanged. The resolver's default layer is 'high'.
autoDecisions.rationale: The rule already says what the resolver implements. Frontmatter stops deciding launches once callers pass a resolved effort.

autoDecisions.summary: Split supportedEffortLevels, clampEffort and effortConfigErrors into a leaf module, src/lib/agents/effort-support.ts, separate from resolve-effort.ts.
autoDecisions.rationale: src/lib/config-yaml.ts re-exports config-yaml/roles.js, so the config validators cannot import a module that reads config-yaml without forming a cycle that npm run lint:circular rejects. tier-table-types.ts (PAN-4191) is the repo precedent for this split.

Create the effort-support leaf module with clamping and config-error helpers

narrative.Action: PRD W2a and D13. Create src/lib/agents/effort-support.ts importing only @overdeck/contracts, ../model-capabilities.js, and `import type` from ../runtimes/types.js (never config-yaml, projects, or resolve-effort). Export supportedEffortLevels(model?, harness?), which intersects getModelEffortLevels(model) (undefined or [] = all five) with getHarnessBehavior(harness).effortLevels (undefined = all five). Export clampEffort(requested, model?, harness?) -> { effort, clamped, warning? }, following the D6 rule: keep the level if supported, else use the highest supported level below it, else the lowest supported level. When the set is empty, keep the requested level and add a warning. The warning text is `Effort '<requested>' is not supported by <model>/<harness>; using '<effort>'.`. Export effortConfigErrors(fieldPath, effort, models), whose messages must be byte-identical to today's settings-api.ts strings. The leaf exists so that config-yaml/roles.ts, settings-api.ts and tier-table.ts can validate effort without importing resolve-effort.ts: config-yaml.ts re-exports config-yaml/roles.js, so that import would create a cycle. Create src/lib/agents/__tests__/resolve-effort.test.ts with a describe('effort-support') block holding the clamping rows (mock ../../model-capabilities.js) and the three effortConfigErrors message rows.

Create resolveEffort with the full precedence chain on top of the effort-support leaf

expected_outputs: resolve-effort.test.ts passes with every precedence row

narrative.Action: PRD W2b. Create src/lib/agents/resolve-effort.ts exporting ResolveEffortInput, ResolvedEffort {effort, source, requested, clamped, warning?}, InvalidEffortError and resolveEffort as specified in the PRD. It imports clampEffort from ./effort-support.js and may import ../config-yaml.js (loadConfigSync default when input.config is absent) and ../projects.js. Precedence: explicit > item > plan > tier(tierName) > sub-role > role > project > default 'high'. An invalid explicit value throws InvalidEffortError. Invalid item, plan or project values fall through (a project value also adds a warning). Project lookup: resolveProjectFromIssueSync(issueId).projectKey, then loadProjectsConfigSync().projects[key]?.effort, in try/catch. Then clamp through clampEffort(requested, model, harness). The module is synchronous and spawns no child processes. Add a describe('resolveEffort') block to src/lib/agents/__tests__/resolve-effort.test.ts with it.each rows: one per precedence layer, the all-empty default row, the invalid-explicit throw, invalid itemEffort fall-through, one clamp-through row, and a `role: 'work', explicit: 'max'` row on a model without max (the pan start shape).
